title: Internal and External Stakeholders
page_title: Internal and External Stakeholders | Cambridge (CIE) AS Business Revision Notes 2022

blocks.md: - A **stakeholder** is **any person, group, or organisation** that has an **interest in or is affected by** the activities and decisions of a business

blocks.alt: Diagram of business stakeholders, showing owners, employees, customers, government, suppliers, managers, local community, and pressure groups.
blocks.caption: Stakeholders are individuals or groups with an interest in the activities of a business

blocks.md:
- A business needs to take into account the **needs and interests of its stakeholders** in order to operate successfully and ensure long term success
- Different stakeholders may have different priorities, which means that at times, it may be difficult for the business to please all stakeholders
- An **internal stakeholder** is someone who is **directly involved inside the organisation** and is affected by its day-to-day operations and decisions

- Provide capital and take overall responsibility for the business
- Invest in a company by buying shares

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** | |---|---| | - Right to profits, right to make decisions (especially in small firms), right to close the business
- Right to *dividends*, vote at *AGM*s, access to key financial info | - Run the business ethically and legally, reinvest or distribute profits, ensure long-term success
- Vote responsibly, monitor company performance, support long-term growth |
- Work in the business and carry out tasks assigned to them

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to fair pay, safe working conditions, job security, non-*discrimination* | - Work effectively, follow company rules, respect colleagues and customers |
- Lead teams and run daily operations

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to make decisions within their department or branch | - Meet targets, manage people and resources, report to senior leaders |
- An **external stakeholder** is a person or group **outside the business** who is affected by or has an interest in its activities and performance
- Purchase and use goods or services

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to safe, good-quality products, fair prices, clear information | - Use products correctly, pay on time, give feedback |
- Provide goods, materials or services needed for production

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to be paid on time, fair contracts, clear communication | - Deliver on time, maintain quality, be reliable |
- Lend money or provide trade credit to the business

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to be repaid on time, to receive *interest*, if agreed | - Provide funds as agreed; assess business risk before lending |

- Lives near or is affected by the business’s operations
- May be employed by the business

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to clean environment, jobs, reduced noise and traffic | - Participate in consultations, give feedback, support local business where possible |
- Regulates business activity, collects tax and sets laws

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to collect taxes, inspect for *compliance*, enforce regulations | - Enforce laws fairly, support economic stability, provide public services |
- Campaign to influence business behaviour, especially on social issues

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to protest, raise awareness, organise campaigns | - Act lawfully, communicate concerns clearly, represent public or *ethical views* |
- Offer similar products and services in the same market

| **Rights** | **Responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| - Right to compete fairly and legally | - Compete ethically; avoid misleading advertising or copying innovations |
